opportunities.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
opportunities.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles.

opportunities.title: Properly size images
opportunities.description: Serve images that are appropriately-sized to save cellular data and improve load time.

opportunities.title: Serve images in next-gen formats
opportunities.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption.

opportunities.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
opportunities.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity.

opportunities.title: Reduce unused CSS
opportunities.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity.

opportunities.title: Minimize main-thread work
opportunities.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this.

opportunities.title: Avoid excessive DOM size
opportunities.description: A large DOM will increase memory usage, cause longer style calculations, and produce costly layout reflows.

opportunities.title: Preconnect to required origins
opportunities.description: Consider adding preconnect or dns-prefetch resource hints to establish early connections to important third-party origins.

_note: This is pre-baked fallback data for when PAGESPEED_API_KEY is not set. Replace with live data by running the orchestrator with a valid API key.
